metadata.title: fix(auth): update API token last_used for MCP Streamable HTTP requests
metadata.author: kimsehwan96

description:
## 🔗 Related Issue
Closes #4027

---

## 📝 Summary

API token last_used timestamps are not updated when accessing Virtual Servers via MCP Streamable HTTP transport (/servers/{id}/mcp). The MCP-specific auth handler (_StreamableHttpAuthHandler._auth_jwt) performs its own JWT verification but omits _update_api_token_last_used_sync() and hardcodes auth_method to "jwt", preventing both timestamp tracking and TokenUsageMiddleware logging for API token requests on MCP paths.

This PR:
- Detects API tokens (via auth_provider claim and legacy DB fallback) in the MCP auth path
- Calls _update_api_token_last_used_sync() for API tokens (reuses existing rate-limited implementation)
- Sets auth_method dynamically ("api_token" vs "jwt") instead of hardcoding
- Propagates auth_method, jti, and user_email to ASGI scope state for TokenUsageMiddleware

---

## 📓 Notes (optional)

The codebase has two independent auth paths:
  1. AuthContextMiddleware (BaseHTTPMiddleware) — handles regular API routes, calls get_current_user() which updates last_used
  2. _StreamableHttpAuthHandler (raw ASGI) — handles MCP transport paths, calls verify_credentials() only

Path 2 was implemented separately because BaseHTTPMiddleware has known issues with SSE streaming responses. It duplicates most auth functionality (JWT verification, revocation, team membership, auth cache) but omitted last_used tracking and API token classification. This PR completes the missing functionality in Path 2.

Test coverage:
- 7 unit tests covering: API token detection, last_used call, session token non-update, failure resilience, legacy token fallback, scope state propagation
- 2 E2E tests (playwright): last_used update verification and usage log recording via live MCP transport

commits.message:
fix(auth): update API token last_used for MCP Streamable HTTP requests

The MCP-specific auth handler (_StreamableHttpAuthHandler._auth_jwt)
performs its own JWT verification via verify_credentials() but did not
call _update_api_token_last_used_sync(), causing API token last_used
timestamps to remain stale when accessing virtual servers via
/servers/{id}/mcp.

Additionally, auth_method was hardcoded to "jwt" regardless of token
type, preventing TokenUsageMiddleware from recognising and logging
API token requests on MCP transport paths.

Changes:
- Detect API tokens (auth_provider == "api_token") and legacy tokens
  (DB JTI lookup) in _auth_jwt()
- Call _update_api_token_last_used_sync() for API tokens (rate-limited)
- Set auth_method dynamically ("api_token" vs "jwt")
- Propagate auth_method, jti, and user_email to ASGI scope state for
  TokenUsageMiddleware
